paper.title: Fine-tuning Neural Network Quantum States
paper.authors: Riccardo Rende, Sebastian Goldt, Federico Becca, Luciano Loris Viteritti

results.system_description: J₁–J₂ Heisenberg, L = 100 · J₂/J₁ = 0.1 · periodic · Sz = 0. H = J1 sum_<ij> S_i · S_j + J2 sum_<<ij>> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J1 = 1; J2 = 0.1; no constant shift
results.variant: Factored attention with RBM output layer, trained from scratch at each J2/J1
results.source_location: Table tab:energies (main.tex l.141-155), row J2/J1 = 0.10 (l.146), column ViT
results.eligibility_evidence: Variational ground-state energy per site of the ViT trained from scratch at this coupling (Table tab:energies); the DMRG column is a reference, and the fine-tuning column is another state (pretrained at J2/J1 = 0.4, output layer re-optimized).
results.notes: The caption of tab:energies states: 'For both instances involving ViT, one trained from scratch and another pretrained at J_2/J_1=0.4 followed by fine-tuning, the Monte Carlo error attributed to finite sampling effects affects the last digit of the reported results.' Recorded as one unit in the last printed digit, with its meaning unspecified (decision P1 of 2026-11-02). Spin-1/2 operators (Eq. J1J2_ham), N = 100 sites with periodic boundaries (Sec. 'The one-dimensional J1-J2 Heisenberg model'). A ViT with factored attention feeds an RBM output layer with complex parameters (Eq. rbm); the hyperparameters of the runs from scratch are not stated separately (the network pretrained in the same section has h = 12, d = 192, n_l = 4, and the states have about 10^6 parameters). Observables are estimated with M = 3000 samples. The magnetization sector is not stated. Below the DMRG energy -0.425417395 of the same row by 5 x 10^-9, within the stated error.
